name: Ansys, Inc. (now part of Synopsys)
origin_detail: Founded in 1970 as Swanson Analysis Systems, Inc. by John Swanson in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, after Westinghouse Astronuclear Laboratory declined his idea; Westinghouse became the first user. Swanson sold his majority interest to TA Associates in 1994; renamed Ansys in 1995; NASDAQ IPO 1996; acquired by Synopsys in July 2025.
openness_notes: Proprietary commercial simulation software throughout its history.

exit_events.note: Founder sold majority interest to the venture/private-equity firm; value not found
Value is approximate amount raised, not market cap
Announced 16 Jan 2024 ($197 cash + 0.3450 SNPS shares per Ansys share; ~$35B enterprise value at 21 Dec 2023 prices); completed 17 Jul 2025

risk_events: 28 May 2025: FTC consent order required divestiture of Ansys PowerArtist (plus Synopsys optical and photonic tools) to Keysight as a condition of the merger; EU, UK and China reviews also required.
Nov 2025: reports that Synopsys would cut about 10% of its workforce and close sites in post-acquisition restructuring, largely in fiscal 2026.
Absorption into a chip-design (EDA) company: first joint product was 'multiphysics fusion' EDA software (Mar 2026), signalling a shift of focus toward semiconductor and AI-chip design.
robustness: Commercially very robust (55 years, $2.54B revenue in 2024) but entirely vendor-controlled; product direction now set by Synopsys's EDA strategy. Users have no fork rights; open alternatives exist only for parts of the portfolio (e.g. OpenFOAM for CFD).
physical_science_relevance: Dominant commercial engineering-simulation suite for structural, fluid, thermal and electromagnetic physics used across aerospace, energy, automotive and semiconductor engineering.
openness_effect_assessment: Ansys never opened its core products; value accrued to shareholders through an IPO and a ~$35B sale rather than to a commons. Closed licensing produced a high-revenue, high-valuation business, but the community has no recourse if the acquirer reprioritises products, which the FTC divestitures and post-merger restructuring illustrate.
key_takeaway: Ansys is the high-water mark for closed physical-science software value: a 1970 founder startup that became a $35B acquisition. Its trajectory (VC buyout, IPO, strategic sale to an EDA firm) is the commercial template against which open simulation infrastructure such as OpenFOAM and LAMMPS can be compared: far more capital captured, but control concentrated in a single owner.
